newsitem.title: USA: Bosnia warns of new "Munich" in key town decision.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia warns of new "Munich" in key town decision.

text.p: Ejup Ganic, vice president of Bosnia, said on Wednesday that giving Serbs control of the strategic Bosnian town of Brcko could lead to more "ethnic cleansing" in central Europe.

"We hope that Munich will not be repeated," Ganic told reporters after talks on the thorny issue of Brcko with Clinton administration officials. He referred to British Foreign Minister Neville Chamberlain's 1939 meeting in Munich that led to the Czech capitulation to Nazi Germany.

An international arbitration board is considering turning control of the Sava river port over to Bosnian Serbs whose separatist forces seized it in May 1992 after a bloody expulsion programme led to thousands of deaths during the 43-month war. The board, based in Rome, is to issue its finding by Feb. 15. American lawyer Roberts Owen is chairman.

Brcko, which once had a majority population of Croats and Moslems, now is home to about 30,000 people, almost all Serb, many of whom are refugees from elsewhere in Bosnia, including some who were driven from Sarajevo, 75 miles (120 km) south.
"Helping dictators to have an ethnically cleansed area will send a bad message," Ganic said. "These people will not stop there ... they will know that genocide and ethnic cleansing are profitable."

Ganic said Brcko should be made part of the Moslem-Croat federation, which would keep it open for everyone to travel through. The town on the border with Croatia provides the most important northern road, rail and water passageway for Bosnia into central and western Europe.
Bosnia's Serbs, who need the town as a corridor to move from their saddle-shaped eastern and western sides, have threatened to go back to war if they lose it.

The Sarajevo government fears that the Clinton administration has decided to give the Serbs control of Brcko but allow the Moslem-Croat federation some port rights, enforced by an international monitoring force.
